candidate_relations.reason: Vagus and glossopharyngeal enhancement could produce cranial neuropathic symptoms, but the presenting complaint was hiccups and CSF proved clonal lymphoma.
CSF flow cytometry established a κ-restricted B-cell lymphoma, but this label omits plasmacytic differentiation and leptomeningeal localization.
Diffuse meningeal enhancement and malignant CSF cells establish leptomeningeal lymphoma, while the lymphoplasmacytic subtype is missing.
Bilateral vagus nerve enhancement may explain the intractable hiccups, but nerve dysfunction is a consequence of meningeal lymphoma rather than the neoplasm itself.
The MRI showed nodular cranial-nerve and diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement with clonal malignant B cells, not the sagging-brain pattern of intracranial hypotension.
Prior rituximab was part of lymphoma therapy, and the record provides no evidence that it caused a new secondary lymphoma.
Malignant B cells in CSF and cranial leptomeningeal enhancement establish CNS lymphoma, but the label lacks the LPL histotype and meningeal pattern.
The history of prior systemic lymphoma chemotherapy and autologous transplant conflicts with calling the current meningeal disease primary CNS lymphoma.
Direct κ-restricted lymphoma cells in CSF demonstrate neoplastic meningeal infiltration rather than a remote paraneoplastic syndrome.
No mediastinal mass is reported, while the disease is demonstrated in CSF with plasmacytic differentiation.
The record shows free malignant cells in CSF and leptomeningeal enhancement, not intravascular large B-cell proliferation in small vessels.
Prior chemotherapy and transplant make relapse plausible, but relapsed lymphoma omits both the leptomeningeal compartment and lymphoplasmacytic identity.

candidate_relations.reason: Flow cytometry specifically found B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation, but this label does not include its leptomeningeal disease site.
Diffuse leptomeningeal and cranial-nerve enhancement with lymphoma cells in CSF supports neoplastic meningitis due to lymphoma, but not its lymphoplasmacytic specification.
The imaging pattern is leptomeningeal malignant spread, yet the generic metastasis label does not identify the κ-restricted lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma.
No large-cell morphology or other evidence of transformation is reported; CSF instead shows plasmacytoid lymphocytes.
Rituximab exposure preceded the current presentation, but there is no causal evidence for a rituximab-related lymphoma.
The previously treated lymphoma and current CSF involvement are compatible with secondary CNS lymphoma, but the candidate omits the leptomeningeal LPL subtype.
The clonal CSF disease is a recurrence pattern of lymphoma, with no record evidence tying its pathogenesis to rituximab-induced lymphoproliferation.
Lymphomatous meningitis fits the diffuse enhancement and malignant CSF population, but does not specify lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma.
